correctness.rationale: Verified the return in the stated original positive-y section, not in an unspecified normal-form radius. For X=y=rC, Y=x=r²S, the angular clock is r(1−r⁷B_m)>0 locally, and at C=1, S=0 the section coordinate is exactly r. Independently expand r(θ)=ρ[1+c₁ρ⁷+c₂ρ¹⁴+c₃ρ²¹+…] in the radial equation. At m=1/3 this gives c₁=F, c₂=4F²+∫₀^θ AB, and c₃′=A(8c₂+28F²+15FB+B²). F vanishes at the two section ends and ∫AB=0 by reflection; integration by parts therefore gives c₃(T)=∫A(B²+7BF). In a separate exact rational calculation, expanding the beta-integrand numerator yielded coefficients (−36,225,−717,1521,−2181,2395,−1823,979,−363) in ascending order; dividing by 1152 and summing against (3/4)_j/(5/4)_j gave 158/49725. This reproduces the positive coefficient, its ρ²² power, and the O(ρ²⁹) remainder by analyticity. The linear coefficient at ρ⁸ is K(m−1/3), where K/T=15/77. Rescaling r=δ^(1/14)R gives the simple positive zero of −K+IR¹⁴ in C¹ and a return multiplier 1+14Iρ²¹+o(ρ²¹)>1. Integrating the actual reciprocal angular speed gives the physical period T/ρ(1+o(1)). Small sections exist uniformly near the threshold and remain transverse; the positive critical displacement implies local repulsion. The frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; their finite sample integrations are corroboration only.
